title: TDS on FD interest for senior citizens
text: For senior citizens, a bank deducts TDS on FD interest only when the interest from that bank crosses Rs 1 lakh in a financial year (the limit was Rs 50,000 before FY 2025-26). TDS is only tax paid in advance. Whether you finally owe tax depends on your total income, tax regime and deductions.

title: Form 15H and Form 121 (stop TDS)
text: Seniors whose total tax for the year will be nil used to give Form 15H to the bank so that no TDS is cut on interest. From FY 2026-27, reports say Form 121 replaces both Form 15G and Form 15H under the Income-tax Act 2025. Please ask your bank which form it accepts.

title: Deduction on interest income for seniors (earlier Section 80TTB)
text: Senior citizens (60 and above) could claim a deduction on interest from savings accounts, FDs, RDs and post office deposits. It was Rs 50,000 until FY 2025-26 and is reported to be Rs 1 lakh from FY 2026-27 (Budget 2026). It is generally an old-regime deduction. Section numbers changed under the new Income-tax Act 2025, so confirm on the official site.

title: Basic exemption limit and tax regimes
text: Under the new regime the basic exemption limit is Rs 4 lakh for all ages. Under the old regime it is Rs 3 lakh for ages 60 to 79 and Rs 5 lakh for age 80 and above. Reports say Budget 2026 did not change slabs for FY 2026-27. Pension gets a standard deduction. Which regime is better depends on your deductions.

title: New Income-tax Act 2025 (from 1 April 2026)
text: The Income-tax Act 2025 applies from 1 April 2026 and replaces the 1961 Act. 'Tax Year' replaces 'Financial Year' and 'Assessment Year', and old section numbers such as 80C or 80TTB have new numbers. Returns for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) are still handled under the 1961 Act.

title: What are Form 16, AIS and ITR
text: Form 16 is a certificate from the payer (employer or pension payer) showing income paid and TDS deducted. AIS (Annual Information Statement) is a summary of your interest, TDS and other transactions reported to the tax department; check it on the e-filing portal before filing. ITR is the Income Tax Return you file to report income and claim refunds. Some senior citizens aged 75 and above with only pension and interest from one bank may be exempt from filing under specified conditions.
